title: LangGraph reference profile operational closure without claiming cross-runtime completion
decision: Keep R05 blocked and formal Gate B/S4 unqualified until the OpenClaw host supplies the required atomic gate and authoritative invocation-start capability. Narrow the active R05 allocation to that residual host-capability surface. The already verified LangGraph RTE-05 contract is sufficient for FE08 and I02A implementation, so their direct R05 start edges are non-blocking. CT04 owns the shared Core models, Guard API wiring, and LangGraph adapter needed to make the reference-runtime Context Builder real. Correct C10 from a non-claimable gate kind to a claimable task kind while retaining its task and gate roles; C10 produces pre-enable evidence but does not turn Gate B green by itself.
rationale: The product target is an honest LangGraph Operational MVP: current/legacy remains official, V2 remains shadow, Context isolation changes real model input, and runtime evidence closes for the reference runtime. Retaining broad R05 reservations after its only remaining blocker became OpenClaw-specific would prevent unrelated verified LangGraph and Context work without improving formal assurance. The direct R05 exit edges to Gate B and S4 remain unchanged, so this decision cannot be read as formal cross-runtime completion.
